scenario: When a new email arrives in the shared support@ Gmail inbox, the agent reads the subject and body, creates a Zendesk ticket tagged with a product-area category (billing, login, shipping, bug), and assigns it to the matching group.
rule_hooks: keyword-to-category mapping table, group ownership per category

scenario: For each new Freshdesk ticket, the agent looks up the requester's company in Salesforce and, if the account is on the Enterprise tier or above a revenue threshold, sets priority to Urgent and assigns the named account's support lead.
rule_hooks: account tier and ARR thresholds, named support lead per account

scenario: Every hour the agent scans open Zendesk tickets, computes time remaining against the first-response SLA for each priority level, and reassigns at-risk tickets to the on-duty escalation queue while posting a summary in the #support-escalations Slack channel.
rule_hooks: SLA response targets per priority, at-risk time buffer

scenario: When a ticket is tagged refund_request, the agent reads the order amount from Shopify and either applies an auto-approve macro, routes the ticket to a team lead, or routes it to finance for approval, depending on the amount.
rule_hooks: refund amount approval tiers, auto-approve limit

scenario: Each submission of the returns Google Form is read; the agent checks the purchase date against the return window, creates an RMA row in the Returns Google Sheet when eligible, and replies to the customer with either an approval and RMA number or a policy-based denial.
rule_hooks: return window days, non-returnable SKU list

scenario: As new Intercom conversations arrive, the agent detects the customer's language and assigns the conversation to an agent in the matching language pod, falling back to the English queue with a translation tag if no pod covers it.

When a Zendesk ticket is marked as a confirmed bug, the agent searches Jira for an existing issue with the same error signature, links the ticket to it or creates a new Jira bug with severity set from the number of affected customers, and posts the link as an internal note.
rule_hooks: duplicate-matching criteria, severity by affected-customer count

scenario: When a Stripe dispute notification email lands in the billing inbox, the agent finds the customer's ticket history, creates a high-priority ticket for the payments specialist, and logs the dispute deadline in the Chargebacks tracker sheet.
rule_hooks: dispute reason code to owner mapping, evidence deadline

scenario: Each day the agent reads new CSAT survey responses, and for any score of 1 or 2 it reopens the related ticket, assigns it to the original agent's team lead, and notifies them in Slack with the customer's comment.

When an incoming ticket mentions cancellation, downgrade, or a competitor, the agent tags it churn_risk, looks up the account's CSM in HubSpot, creates a HubSpot task for that CSM, and notifies them in Slack.
rule_hooks: churn keyword list, CSM ownership field

scenario: During an active incident posted on the status page, the agent scans new tickets for symptoms that match the incident, links them to a parent problem ticket, applies the outage macro reply, and sets them to pending.
rule_hooks: incident symptom keywords, active incident window

scenario: When an email or ticket reports a vulnerability, account compromise, or phishing, the agent moves it to the restricted Security group, strips it from public views, and pages the security on-call via a PagerDuty incident.

When a ticket requests data deletion or export, the agent classifies it as a GDPR or CCPA request based on the customer's region, logs it in the Privacy Requests sheet with the statutory due date, and assigns it to the privacy officer.
rule_hooks: jurisdiction by customer region, statutory response deadlines

scenario: When a ticket is about an invoice discrepancy, the agent pulls the invoice from QuickBooks, attaches the amount and status as an internal note, and routes the ticket to accounts receivable if the invoice is overdue or to billing support otherwise.

For tickets created outside business hours, the agent sends a timezone-aware acknowledgment with expected response time and, if the requester holds a 24/7 support contract, pages the after-hours on-call engineer instead of queuing the ticket.
rule_hooks: business hours per region, 24/7 contract entitlement list

scenario: As tickets enter the General queue, the agent assigns each to the next agent in rotation, skipping anyone marked out of office on the Google Calendar or already holding more than the open-ticket cap.
rule_hooks: round-robin order, per-agent open ticket cap, OOO calendar

scenario: When the Slack channel fed by social listening posts a brand mention that contains a complaint, the agent creates a Freshdesk ticket tagged social, sets priority by follower count, and assigns it to the social care team.
rule_hooks: complaint detection terms, follower-count priority bands

scenario: When a warranty claim ticket arrives with a serial number, the agent looks up the purchase date and product line in the Warranty Registry sheet, and routes in-warranty claims to replacements, applying the out-of-warranty repair-quote macro to the rest.

For tickets asking where is my order, the agent checks the tracking status, sends the tracking update automatically when the order is in transit within its estimate, and routes lost or overdue shipments to the logistics team to file a carrier claim.
rule_hooks: delivery estimate tolerance, carrier claim eligibility days

scenario: The agent reviews new tickets in the support inbox, closes those that are out-of-office replies, delivery failure bounces, or vendor solicitations with a spam tag, and leaves genuine customer tickets in the queue.

When a customer opens a new ticket while an existing one from the same email about the same order is still open, the agent merges the new ticket into the original and notifies the assigned agent with an internal note.

When a ticket comes from a domain on the reseller list, the agent tags it with the partner name, assigns it to the channel support team, and copies the partner manager listed in Salesforce on the reply.
rule_hooks: reseller domain list, partner manager ownership

scenario: When a ticket is classified as a feature request, the agent logs it in the Feature Requests Airtable base with the account's ARR from Salesforce, replies with the feature-request macro, and solves the ticket.
rule_hooks: feature request classification, ARR lookup for weighting

scenario: For tickets from accounts whose HubSpot close date is within the last 60 days, the agent tags them onboarding and assigns them to that account's implementation specialist rather than the general queue.
rule_hooks: onboarding window days, implementation specialist assignment

scenario: When an incoming message mentions a lawyer, lawsuit, regulator complaint, or BBB filing, the agent suspends any automated replies, assigns the ticket to the support director, and emails the legal team a summary.
rule_hooks: legal-threat trigger phrases, legal notification list

scenario: For each voicemail transcript emailed by the phone system, the agent matches the caller ID to a customer record, creates a callback ticket with the transcript, and schedules it into the callback queue ordered by account tier.

When a customer emails asking to cancel, the agent checks plan and tenure in the billing system, routes annual-plan customers to the retention team with a save-offer flag, and processes monthly-plan cancellations with a confirmation reply.
rule_hooks: plan type and tenure retention rules, eligible save offers

scenario: When a damaged-item ticket arrives, the agent checks for photo attachments, requests photos with a macro if none are attached, and when photos are present creates a replacement order request for items under the replacement cap or routes to a supervisor above it.
rule_hooks: photo evidence requirement, replacement value cap

scenario: When a solved ticket is reopened by the customer for the second time, the agent bumps its priority, reassigns it from tier 1 to the tier 2 queue, and adds a reopen-count tag for quality reporting.
rule_hooks: reopen count threshold, tier escalation path

scenario: Each week the agent reviews solved tickets with no linked help-center article, groups them by topic tag, and creates a Notion task for the knowledge team for any topic that has more than five such tickets.

When an Intercom chat ends unresolved or the customer leaves before an agent replies, the agent converts it into an email ticket in Zendesk with the chat transcript, routes it by the chat's topic attribute, and sends the customer a follow-up email.

The agent watches shared Slack Connect channels with enterprise customers, creates a Zendesk ticket for each message that asks a question or reports a problem, and replies in the thread with the ticket number and the SLA that applies.
rule_hooks: channel-to-account mapping, contract SLA per account

scenario: Tickets that mention API errors, webhook failures, or include stack traces are tagged technical and assigned to the developer support pod, with the customer's plan API rate limits from the admin sheet added as an internal note.
rule_hooks: technical signal patterns, plan rate-limit reference sheet

scenario: When a customer asks for a price match or for a discount that was applied after their purchase, the agent compares the order date against the price-protection window and either applies a credit through the refund macro or replies with the policy denial template.
rule_hooks: price protection window, competitor match policy

scenario: For tickets requesting a password reset, email change, or 2FA removal, the agent checks whether the request came from the email on file, sends the identity verification macro when it did not, and routes verified requests to the account security queue.
rule_hooks: identity verification policy, sensitive change types

scenario: When a customer email is sent or forwarded to an executive address such as the CEO's, the agent creates an urgent ticket tagged exec_escalation, assigns it to the support manager, and requires a response by end of business with a calendar hold.
rule_hooks: executive address list, exec escalation SLA

scenario: For each new ticket from an account whose renewal date in Salesforce falls within the next 90 days, the agent adds a renewal_window tag and CCs the account executive on any ticket of high priority.
rule_hooks: renewal window days, AE ownership, priority threshold

scenario: When customers reply to DocuSign envelope notifications with questions about terms or signing problems, the agent routes contract-term questions to sales ops and signing technical issues to tier 1 support, and links the envelope ID on the ticket.
rule_hooks: contract vs technical question classification, envelope lookup

scenario: Each Monday the agent reads the unassigned and aging ticket backlog in Freshdesk, redistributes tickets older than three days evenly across the agents on shift, and emails the team lead a per-agent reassignment report.
rule_hooks: aging threshold, shift roster, balancing rule

scenario: When a premium customer's ticket asks for a live walkthrough, the agent confirms the account's screen-share entitlement, books a Zoom meeting on an available specialist's calendar, and replies with the invite, or declines politely for non-entitled plans.
rule_hooks: live session entitlement by plan, specialist availability

scenario: When a 'where is my order' email lands in the support inbox, the agent finds the order in Shopify, replies with the carrier tracking link and expected delivery date, and solves the ticket, unless the order is more than 5 days past its promised date, in which case it tags the ticket and assigns it to the fulfillment exceptions queue.

For each new Zendesk ticket from a B2B account, the agent looks up the account's support plan in Salesforce (Basic/Premium/Premier), then sets the matching SLA policy and queue. If the contract has expired, it routes the ticket to a renewals-aware queue and sends a courtesy notice.
rule_hooks: support plan entitlement matrix, contract end date

scenario: Incoming helpdesk tickets that mention a SKU or product model are mapped to a product family using a SKU-to-team Google Sheet and assigned to that family's specialist group. Tickets with no recognizable SKU go to general tier-1.

Pricing or demo questions from non-customers that arrive in the support inbox are turned into HubSpot leads and assigned to the SDR who owns the sender's territory. The support ticket is then closed with a 'connected you with sales' reply.

Emails to support from journalists or media outlets (detected by signature, domain list, or wording) are forwarded to the PR team's Slack channel with a summary. The ticket is closed with a holding reply, and agents are told not to comment.

Supplier invoices and payment-status emails sent to the support address by mistake are detected, forwarded to the accounts-payable inbox with the PDF attached, and closed in Freshdesk with a polite redirect note to the sender.
rule_hooks: vendor master list, AP mailbox routing

scenario: Contact-form submissions that ask about quantities above the wholesale threshold, or that mention reselling, are routed to the B2B sales rep for the submitter's region. The rep gets a Slack DM, and the submitter gets a wholesale catalog reply.

Tickets that request on-site installation or repair are matched by postal code to a field-service region. The agent creates a work order in the dispatch board for that region's coordinator, and offers the customer the next available slots from the team calendar.

When a ticket contains a device serial number, the agent checks it against the active recall range list. Matching tickets are tagged 'recall', assigned to the recall coordinator, and answered with the recall remedy template. Non-matching tickets follow normal routing.

Tickets that describe injury, fire, smoke, or overheating are flagged as safety incidents, set to urgent, and assigned to the quality and regulatory team. The agent also logs an entry in the incident register sheet within the required reporting window.
rule_hooks: safety keyword list, regulatory reporting deadline

scenario: Messages saying 'I didn't place this order' or reporting an unfamiliar charge are matched to the order. If it has not shipped, the agent places a fulfillment hold and routes the ticket to the trust and fraud team. If it has already shipped, it routes the ticket to fraud with a carrier-intercept request.

Tickets about a declined card or failed renewal are matched to the subscription in the billing system. The agent replies with a secure payment-update link and the remaining grace-period days. Accounts already past grace are routed to billing ops for manual reinstatement.

Emails with an attached sales-tax exemption certificate are logged in the tax certificates sheet, the customer record in QuickBooks is flagged pending, and the ticket is assigned to the tax specialist. Certificates that are expired or for an unsupported state get a template asking for a valid form.

Tickets from accounts enrolled in the beta program (from the beta roster sheet) that mention the beta feature are tagged, posted to the product team's #beta-feedback Slack channel, and assigned to the beta liaison instead of regular support.

New App Store and Google Play reviews are pulled daily. 1–2 star reviews that mention a bug become helpdesk tickets assigned to mobile support, and a public response template is drafted. 4–5 star reviews are logged to the advocacy sheet.

Community forum posts that have gone 48 hours without an accepted answer or staff reply are converted into tickets. Each is assigned to the agent whose expertise tags match the post's category, and a link back is posted in the thread.

Requests for nonprofit or education pricing are checked against the eligibility rules: a .edu domain or a registered charity number in the verification sheet. Eligible requests go to billing to apply the discount code. Others get a reply listing the required proof.

Each morning, the agent checks the team's Google Calendar for out-of-office agents. Their open tickets with customer replies waiting are reassigned to their designated backup from the coverage sheet, and an internal note is left on each ticket.

Tickets in 'pending customer' status get a reminder email after 3 days and are solved with a closing message after 7 days. Tickets tagged 'enterprise' or with an open refund are excluded and flagged to the owner instead.

Customer messages containing threats, slurs, or harassment are removed from the agent's view queue, assigned to the team lead, and tagged for policy review. Repeat offenders found in the conduct log get a templated warning or account flag.

Requests to change an account's admin or owner (for example, after an employee leaves) are checked for whether the requester is on the account's authorized-contacts list. Authorized requests go to account ops. Others get a reply asking for a signed authorization letter from the company.
rule_hooks: authorized contacts list, ownership-change proof requirements

scenario: Tickets asking to downgrade a plan mid-term are read for the current plan and term. Monthly plans get self-serve downgrade instructions. Annual contracts are routed to the account manager with a proration estimate, since annual downgrades only take effect at renewal.
rule_hooks: billing term type, mid-term change policy

scenario: Disputes over usage or overage charges are matched to the invoice in Xero. Disputes under $250 are routed to billing support with a suggested one-time credit. Larger ones go to the account manager, along with the usage export attached from the admin sheet.
rule_hooks: dispute amount threshold, credit authority limits

scenario: Customer requests for a SOC 2 report, pen-test summary, or security questionnaire are checked for whether an NDA is on file in Salesforce. Requests with an NDA are routed to the security team queue. Those without get an NDA sent through DocuSign first.

When the tier-1 queue exceeds 300 open tickets or the median first-response time passes 6 hours, new tickets in the approved categories (order status, password reset, address change) are routed to the outsourced BPO group instead of in-house agents.

When account executives post customer problems in the internal #support-escalations Slack channel, the agent creates a ticket linked to the Salesforce account. Priority is set from the account's ARR band, and the ticket link is posted back in the thread.

Address-change requests are checked against the order's fulfillment status. If the order has not been picked, the agent updates the address in Shopify and confirms. If it has been picked, the request goes to the warehouse team. If it has shipped, the customer gets carrier redirect instructions.

Reports that an item was missing from a delivered order are compared with the packing-slip weight and pick records in the warehouse sheet. If the records confirm a short pick, a replacement is shipped automatically. If the records show complete, the case goes to the warehouse lead for investigation.

For a regulated financial product, tickets that meet the definition of a formal complaint (expressing dissatisfaction and asking for remedy) are logged in the complaints register. The agent sends the required acknowledgment within 24 hours and assigns the case to the complaints officer, with the 8-week final-response deadline set as the due date.
rule_hooks: regulatory complaint definition, statutory response deadlines

scenario: Messages reporting that an account holder has died are routed to the specialized bereavement team. Marketing emails to the account are paused in HubSpot, billing is placed on hold, and a compassionate template listing required documents is sent.

Requests for accessible formats or accommodations (large-print documents, screen-reader help, sign-language video calls) are tagged and assigned to the accessibility-trained agent group, with a 1-business-day response target.

Subpoenas, police data requests, and emergency disclosure requests that arrive by email are isolated from general queues and assigned to legal operations. The sender's agency domain is logged, and the legally required response deadline is recorded.

Tickets from free-plan users are answered with the most relevant help-center articles and community link, set to low priority, and placed in the self-serve queue. Billing or account-lockout issues are exempt and still go to tier-1.

Emails arriving at the company's several brand support addresses are assigned to the matching brand group in the helpdesk. Each gets the brand's signature and macros, and orders are looked up in the correct brand's store.

Each week, the agent samples recently solved tickets per agent (more for new hires, plus every ticket with negative CSAT) and assigns them to QA reviewers in the scorecard sheet, balancing reviewer workload.

Tickets that tier-1 escalates to tier 2 are checked for required fields: steps to reproduce, account ID, logs attached, and troubleshooting already tried. Incomplete escalations are returned to the original agent with a note listing what is missing.

Text messages to the support number are matched to a customer by phone number in the CRM. Messages from known customers are threaded into their open ticket or create a new one. Unknown numbers get an auto-text asking for an order number.

Wrong-item complaints are checked against the order line items. If the customer's photo or description matches a known mis-pick SKU pair from the warehouse log, the agent issues a return label and a replacement. Otherwise it routes the case to returns review.

Tickets about apps or plugins built by marketplace developers (identified from the marketplace listing sheet) get a reply with the developer's support contact. The ticket is closed, unless the issue involves the core platform's API, in which case it goes to the integrations team.
rule_hooks: marketplace app ownership list, platform-vs-vendor boundary
